questions.text: How does masked discrete image generation differ from strictly autoregressive image-token generation?

options.A: It predicts continuous pixel noise instead of using discrete image tokens.
options.B: It fills multiple masked image-token positions in parallel over successive rounds.
options.C: It predicts each image token once in a fixed left-to-right order.
options.D: It generates text captions and never predicts image-token IDs.

questions.explanation: Masked discrete generation predicts multiple missing image codes per round, then progressively commits predictions instead of decoding every image code sequentially.

questions.text: How would you apply a masked-token image generator to inpainting while preserving the visible region?

options.A: Mask the entire image and remove all visible-region conditioning.
options.B: Convert visible image codes into text and use only text next-token prediction.
options.C: Freeze all masked positions and generate only the already visible positions.
options.D: Keep known-region codes as context and predict codes for the masked region.

questions.explanation: Inpainting conditions on the known image-token region while filling the unknown masked region, using the masked-prediction mechanism.

questions.text: step_unmask computes n_to_keep=max(1, int(len(masked_indices)*keep_ratio)). With 5 masked positions and keep_ratio=0.15, how many are filled this step?
questions.explanation: int(5×0.15)=int(0.75)=0, but max(1,0)=1 ensures at least one masked position is filled.
